summary: Main interface to a Luxonis OAK camera, combining device/pipeline lifecycle controls, Timer-style status channels, callbacks, and TOP-to-device stream input.

key_concepts: OAK Device CHOP is the main TouchDesigner interface to an OAK camera.
It implements Timer CHOP-like counters, pulses, and custom Python callbacks.
The createPipeline callback defines the DepthAI pipeline before the camera is started.
Play controls whether newly received OAK messages are processed by downstream OAK Select operators.
The Stream In page can send RGBA 8-bit TOP images from TouchDesigner to an OAK XLinkIn stream, converted to BGR.
Output parameters expose initialization, ready, running, done, failure, and timer-style state channels.
common_gotchas: Connect OAK devices before starting TouchDesigner when possible; otherwise pulse Refresh Sensor List after connecting.
Customize the Python createPipeline callback before starting the camera.
Saving a project while the camera is running can cause the camera to auto-start when the project opens.
Resolution and ISP scale choices must be compatible with the specific OAK hardware.
Turning Play off freezes downstream OAK Select CHOP/TOP operators on their most recently received message.
When sending TOP images to OAK, TouchDesigner converts to BGR; use a DepthAI ImageManip node if another format is required.
FPS targets are generally selected when the DepthAI pipeline loads and may not change live.
